name: FORK
oneLine: The social network where trading ideas evolve in public.
description:
FORK is the social network where trading ideas evolve in public. A trader publishes a thesis; another trader forks it, changes the approach and preserves the original author, parent idea and independent authorship. The Idea Tree makes that contribution history visible.

The live demonstration contains two real Privy users, an ETH root thesis #1 and its independently authored fork #2. The fork changes the target from 4200 to 4400 and leverage from 2x to 3x. Both publications are real Monad Testnet transactions, indexed by Envio HyperIndex. Judges can inspect the lineage, parameter and reasoning differences, contributor profiles, an Agree and a comment without signing in. Profiles show deterministic contribution formulas and Emerging labels for the small sample; this is demonstration evidence, not adoption or trading performance.

FORK fits Track 03 because the core interaction is collaborative authorship and public attribution. Trading is the subject of the conversation; the product is a persistent social contribution graph. There is no live token, revenue sharing or economic reward.

Privy supplies Google authentication and user-controlled embedded EVM wallets. Wallets sign publications directly to FORKRegistry on Monad Testnet (chain 10143). Envio indexes the contract events for public discovery and lineage. Next.js serves the product, and standard PostgreSQL stores verified identity associations, metadata and offchain social interactions. Envio does not verify trades. The production app runs behind HTTPS with private PostgreSQL.

Perpl execution is deferred pending Origin approval; no trade execution is claimed. Nansen enrichment is deferred because provider API access is unavailable. Next steps are a small trader-community pilot, collecting feedback on useful contributions, and completing independent execution verification when provider access permits.

Project history: the repository begins on October 4, 2026 within the hackathon build window. External frameworks, libraries and provider services are attributed in the README. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, tests, documentation and submission preparation; the human project owner reviewed and approved the product gates.
goToMarket:
Start with a small, invited cohort of traders who already explain ideas in public and people who regularly improve those ideas. The initial workflow is to share a root thesis link, invite an alternative approach and review the resulting Idea Tree together. Public read access lets readers inspect the contribution before choosing to sign in.

Recruit this first cohort through direct outreach and demonstrations in relevant Monad and trading communities. These are planned activities, not existing partnerships or a launched acquisition program. Publish short examples of how a changed target, leverage or rationale remains attributable, and ask contributors whether the graph is more useful than a comment thread.

Measure repeat contributions, independent forks, return visits and qualitative usefulness before expanding. The current proof has two users and one fork; no audience size, revenue or organic growth is claimed. Prioritize dependable social reads and clear authorship. Evaluate creator incentives only after validating repeated use; no token or rewards are implemented.

Existing root #1 and fork #2 are real Monad Testnet publications. Agree/comment state is visible on root #1. Google login uses Privy and creates or reuses a user-controlled embedded EVM wallet. No judge credentials are supplied or required for read-only review. Publishing needs testnet MON and a wallet approval; the existing evidence is sufficient for review without a new transaction. Perpl and Nansen are deferred. If an upstream read temporarily fails, use the visible Retry action.
envio:
Envio HyperIndex 3.12.1 runs on Envio Cloud and indexes FORKRegistry on Monad Testnet 10143 from deployment block 69535255. Registry ThesisCreated events become the public thesis/parent graph and handler-maintained lineage counters used by the live Feed, thesis pages, Idea Tree and deterministic profiles. These are core product reads, not a decorative integration.

The real root #1 and independently authored fork #2 are indexed and visible at https://forktrades.xyz/t/2/tree. The fork retains parent #1 and changes target 4200 to 4400 and leverage 2x to 3x. Public GraphQL: https://indexer.dev.hyperindex.xyz/da86abe/v1/graphql. The repository includes indexer/config.yaml, indexer/schema.graphql and indexer/src/handlers/registry.ts with 12 handler tests.

PostgreSQL stores offchain metadata and comments. The application checks metadata commitments against indexed data before calling it trusted. Envio does not verify Perpl trades, and no execution is claimed. The deployment is a live development-tier Cloud endpoint; no separate production-tier indexer is claimed.
privy:
Privy powers Google authentication and persistent, user-controlled embedded EVM wallets. The two real demonstration users used their embedded wallets to sign independent original and fork publications to FORKRegistry on Monad Testnet. This is beyond a login-only integration: the wallet is the onchain author of the idea and approves the publication transaction.

Existing proofs include root #1 transaction 0xbcbfa028b4078a97cf1198d4ffac2f61691d8ac0607b43a006a6595b630a090f and fork #2 transaction 0xe5fbf9c835109a566be8afebd5c2d146731d1f998851ea1875798e328ab6b192. https://forktrades.xyz/t/2/tree exposes the independently authored lineage.

The server verifies Privy access tokens, fetches authoritative linked wallets, checks the selected primary wallet and stores the association transactionally in PostgreSQL. Approved production evidence covers Google logout/login persistence, the same embedded wallet, server-side identity association and unauthenticated/wrong-wallet rejection. No wallet private keys are stored on the server.

The video and evidence distinguish existing signed transactions from any fresh transaction; this submission preparation does not create a new publication or trade. See docs/evidence/phase3/PRIVY.md, PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT.md and SOCIAL_JOURNEY.md for the recorded gates.
